target_customer: Underbanked individuals and micro merchants in Peru's informal economy
problem: People in the informal economy have no credit history and little access to formal loans; the founders aim to underwrite them with phone data and a network of endorsers.
business_model: Consumer nano loans (S/50 to S/800, 30 day term) with interest, plus a digital wallet

founders.name: Christophe Robilliard
founders.background_notes: YC page describes him as an engineer and lists McKinsey consultant, Easy Taxi GM, Cabify regional manager, Ligo COO. Forbes Peru says he was an Easy Taxi manager at age 23 and calls him an industrial engineer; no age_at_founding recorded.

founders.name: Jose Manuel Palacios
founders.background_notes: Per Forbes Peru: regional product manager at Easy Taxi and regional software and data manager at Cabify.

competitors.name: Yape
competitors.what: BCP's digital wallet in Peru, which announced microcredits of S/150 to S/200 in 2022
competitors.traction_then: Interoperable with Plin, Tunki, Lukita and BIM; planned 60,000 microcredits in three months
competitors.funding_then: Owned by Banco de Credito del Peru

competitors.name: Apurata
competitors.what: Peruvian digital credit platform aimed at the middle class

technical_complexity.rationale: Credit scoring on 250+ phone and bureau variables and a wallet need data science and compliance, but no research grade problem.

defensibility.rationale: Repayment data on a thin file population can compound, but lending is copyable and funding cost drives competitiveness.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Yape entered microcredit in 2022; no sourced acquisition of Kashin.

market_need_then: Launch post says default rates in this segment are around 15 percent traditionally versus Kashin's under 8 percent claim; the company reports 10K users and nearly 2M USD annualized revenue at batch time.

identity.voice_and_tone: Friendly, informal and reassuring; uses tu, emojis and the tagline 'Estas en buenas manos'.

branding.brand_signature: Tagline Estas en buenas manos and a ladder loan program
branding.community_and_virality: Referral bonus program on the website; no independent community evidence found.

brand_strength.rationale: Friendly voice but little press or community evidence about the brand itself.

outcome_analysis: Kashin, founded in Peru in 2020 by two ex Easy Taxi and Cabify executives, joined YC in Summer 2022 with small loans to micro merchants. It reports about 2 million dollars of annualized revenue then and was approving more than 1,000 loans a day in 2025 per a Peruvian outlet, and Grupo RPP invested in 2025. It stays active; the funding history is thin in public sources so success is only partly evidenced.
notes: Pre-seed angel syndicate named by Forbes Peru and LatamFintech (both Aug 2022) without date or amount; lending was funded by a 200,000 USD debt fund. They planned to raise over 3M USD in Sept 2022; not confirmed closed. CB Insights lists a 0.5M USD YC convertible note (Aug 2022) and 1.6M USD total; aggregator only, unverified. A third founder 'Tex' appears as a launch post author; identity not confirmed, not recorded as founder. A data aggregator claims an M&A offer in April 2025; unverified. Grupo RPP amount and date unstated beyond the URL date (2025-06-03) and the stage is not stated. Apurata source is an undated comparison page. No shutdown found.
